title: Badge Inspection — Concourse A Kitchen

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority — Security & Law Enforcement
fields.location: Concourse A Kitchen, SkyWay Catering Prep Area
fields.summary: Security Officer S. Rivas located Carlos Mendez, Badge ID 74291, in the Concourse A kitchen at 07:52. Mendez confirmed he has not left the kitchen since 07:04 and was seen by three coworkers during that time. He produced his badge (125 kHz RFID) on lanyard, visually unaltered. Mendez stated he last used the badge at 06:55 for entry to Door S-4 (Concourse A), but verification shows he did not access Door S-4 at 07:38. The badge was scanned at 125 kHz during the 07:38 event, but Mendez’s morning access at 06:55 was at 13.56 MHz. No evidence of physical tampering. The badge appears to be a duplicate.

findings.notes: No visible damage, scratch, or modification to housing or antenna coil
125 kHz scan recorded at 07:38; Mendez’s morning access at 06:55 was 13.56 MHz; same badge cannot operate across both frequencies without modification
Mendez’s badge does not have biometric reader
Badge ID 74291 logged at Door S-4 at 07:38; Mendez was in kitchen from 07:04 to 07:52; no record of actual visit to Door S-4

findings.item: Badge owner presence at time of access
findings.notes: Mendez was confirmed in kitchen by three coworkers; timestamped access to Door S-4 occurred while he was present elsewhere

findings.item: Door S-4 access control system status
findings.notes: Door S-4 logs show green LED and 5-second lock release at 07:38; no forced or held-open alarms

findings.item: CCTV coverage of Door S-4 at 07:38
findings.notes: Video feed from NCIA-VIDEO-A (SEC-NVR-01) is being retrieved by IT team
Three SkyWay Catering staff confirmed Mendez was in kitchen from 07:04 to 07:52
Badge ID 74291 issued to Mendez under C5; verification pending IT
No interference detected; badge operating within expected environment

actionsTaken: Confronted Carlos Mendez at kitchen location
Verified badge presence and visual integrity
Notified IT team via radio (SEC-07 to IT Lead) at 07:52
Documented timestamped events and access patterns
recommendations: IT to analyze badge frequency mismatch and PACS logs for 125 kHz vs 13.56 MHz conflict
Conduct forensic review of SEC-BADGE-01 (NCIA-ENROLL) for duplicate badge creation
Verify badge issuance history via C5 (49 CFR § 1542.211)
Begin CCTV correlation from SEC-NVR-01 for Door S-4 at 07:38
fields.photosNote: 1 photo attached: IMG_20261022_0752_S1 (Security Officer S. Rivas with Carlos Mendez, badge visible on lanyard)

instructorNote: This inject confirms the badge clone. The frequency mismatch (125 kHz vs 13.56 MHz) is a key clue that the badge was not used in its original form. IT should begin forensic analysis of the badge reader logs and biometric workstation.

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Security Program (ASP)
citations.quote: Valid read: green LED, lock releases 5 seconds. Invalid read: red LED, "Access Denied" logged. Door Forced Open alarm; Door Held Open alarm (> 30 s). **Hard Anti-Passback** at the employee portal.

citations.quote: Badges issued to individuals with a legitimate operational need. Possession is a privilege, not a right.
